brief: 6 writing tips for founders who hate writing.

slots.headline: Six Writing Tips for Founders Who Truly Hate Writing

slots.title: Talk, Don't Type
slots.body: Record your thoughts as a voice memo, then transcribe them. Speaking naturally unlocks ideas faster than staring at a blank page. Edit the transcript into clean copy.

slots.title: One Messy Draft
slots.body: Give yourself permission to write badly on the first pass. Perfectionism kills momentum before a single sentence is finished. You can polish raw ideas, but you cannot edit an empty screen.

slots.title: Use Simple Structure
slots.body: Start with the problem, present your solution, then add proof. This three-part framework removes guesswork from every landing page or email. Clarity beats cleverness when you are selling trust.

slots.title: Set a Timer
slots.body: Limit writing sprints to fifteen minutes to silence your inner critic. A tight deadline forces decisions and prevents endless rewriting. You will be surprised how much usable copy appears under pressure.

slots.title: Copy Your Customers
slots.body: Pull phrases from customer reviews, sales calls, and support tickets. Your audience already describes the problem in words that convert. Borrow their language instead of inventing jargon from scratch.

slots.title: Hire an Editor
slots.body: You do not need to be the final polish. Get the ideas down, then hand them to an editor. Great founders delegate refinement so they can keep building.

slots.headline: Turn Thoughts Into Copy
slots.body: Apply these tips today and watch your content finally get finished. Your message matters more than perfect prose.
